title: A pinned file whose cited passages are word for word at the newer commit or release is re-pinned and its facts re-pointed with no model
goal: For a source of kind raw-pin, raw-ref or release in bucket CHANGED or NEWER-VERSION, the census resolves each citing fact's anchor against the file at the newer commit or release from the bare clone (git show, no network beyond the clone fetch); when every citing fact is found word for word, census.py writes the new pinned row through kbid.py add, sets superseded_by on the old row, re-points the citations and records outcome superseded with the proof (old and new commit, facts matched), all in the factdiff apply style with --dry-run and a KB-Verified commit; a source with any fact not found stays in the phase-2 queue with only those facts in its review items. A pinned file with no located anchors stays in the queue unchanged.

gates.question: Where does the no-model re-pin live: a new census.py subcommand repin LOG [--date D] [--dry-run] [--commit] chained into run after check (own KB-Verified commit), or inside check?
options: repin subcommand, chained in run after check
repin subcommand, not chained in run
gates.recommendation: repin subcommand, chained in run after check
gates.answer: repin subcommand, chained in run after check

gates.question: A fact that names the pinned tag (or a tag of the pinned commit) in its text: is it re-pointed when its anchor is found word for word at the newer release, or read by a model?
options: read: counts as not found, the source stays in phase 2
re-pointed like any fact found word for word
gates.recommendation: read: counts as not found, the source stays in phase 2

gates.question: The url of the new pinned row: for NEWER-VERSION the file at the newer tag, for CHANGED (a pin or a branch ref) the file at the newer commit's full sha, or always the commit sha?
options: newer tag url for NEWER-VERSION, commit sha url for CHANGED
gates.recommendation: newer tag url for NEWER-VERSION, commit sha url for CHANGED
gates.answer: newer tag url for NEWER-VERSION, commit sha url for CHANGED

gates.question: A re-point reword changes a fact's key: do anchors and doc2query expansions follow it and the old id leave the article's sources: header, or are they left to anchor, doc2query prune and the next lint?
options: re-key the anchors and expansions and drop the old id from sources: when nothing else names it
leave them to factdiff.py anchor and doc2query.py prune
gates.recommendation: re-key the anchors and expansions and drop the old id from sources: when nothing else names it
gates.answer: re-key the anchors and expansions and drop the old id from sources: when nothing else names it

gates.question: A row of kind release (its url is a release page, not a file): leave it in the queue with the reason, or search the release's tree for the cited passages?
options: leave it in the queue, reason named in the output
search the whole tree of the newer release
gates.recommendation: leave it in the queue, reason named in the output

notes: Premise from kb/public/_census/2026-09-26.csv (tally run 2026-10-10): 13 NEWER-VERSION rows (9 raw-ref at newer=2.2.364, 4 api-repo) and 7 CHANGED raw-pin or raw-ref rows went to phase 2, and all but two came back confirmed, so the model read whole files to find the cited lines unchanged. factdiff.py detect marks pinned sources 'pinned url: its text cannot change' and leaves them to census.py check, so neither tool compares the citing facts against the newer file today.
